faq.q: What is a UGC platform and how is it different from an influencer agency?
faq.a: A UGC platform lets a brand brief creators, receive videos and pay for them in one place, without an agency in the middle. On TrendBag you write the brief yourself, pick creators from those who apply, approve each video and release payment only after approval. You keep direct control over products, rights and budget, and see results per creator.

faq.q: How much does UGC cost in India?
faq.a: There is no single rate. Cost depends on the creator's niche and engagement, how many videos you need, whether you want rights for brand organic use or paid ads, how long those rights last, and the product you ship. On TrendBag you set the ₹ fee per approved video in each brief, and creators decide whether to apply at that fee.

faq.q: Do I need a Shopify store to use TrendBag?
faq.a: TrendBag is built around Shopify, and WooCommerce is also supported. Connecting your store with TrendBag Connect syncs your catalogue so briefs use real products, lets you ship samples as ₹0 orders from your own store, and enables sales attribution through a Shopify Web Pixel on your domain.

faq.q: Can I use creator videos in my Instagram ads?
faq.a: Yes, if the brief includes paid ad rights. When you write a brief you choose creator posts only, brand organic use, or paid ads for a set number of days. That choice becomes a written licence for the job, so both sides know exactly where and for how long the video can run.

faq.q: What happens if I do not like the video a creator delivers?
faq.a: You can request changes, up to two revision rounds per video, before approving. The creator is paid only after you approve. If you do not respond within 72 hours of a delivery, the video is auto-approved, so creators are not left waiting indefinitely for a decision.

faq.q: How do I track sales from influencers on Shopify?
faq.a: Give each creator a unique tracked link and record checkouts on your store. On TrendBag every creator gets a link per product, and a Shopify Web Pixel on your store records the completed checkout using a first-party cookie on your domain. Orders appear on the brief leaderboard against the creator who drove them.

faq.q: Are coupon codes enough to measure influencer sales?
faq.a: Usually not. Codes get shared on deal sites, applied by shoppers who never saw the creator, or forgotten at checkout, so they both over-count and under-count. TrendBag uses tracked links and a Shopify Web Pixel as the main signal, and you can add codes as an optional extra signal.

faq.q: What attribution window does TrendBag use?
faq.a: TrendBag credits an order to the creator whose link was last clicked within 7 days before the purchase. If the order is later refunded or cancelled, that credit is reversed. For posts boosted as Meta partnership ads, view-through results come from Meta's own ad reporting.

faq.q: How do I calculate ROAS for influencer marketing?
faq.a: ROAS is the revenue attributed to a creator divided by what you paid them. TrendBag shows it per creator on each brief's leaderboard, using the fee you set and attributed revenue net of refunds and cancellations, next to views, CPM, link clicks and orders, so you can compare creators on the same brief.

faq.q: Does TrendBag share creator or customer data with Shopify?
faq.a: Attribution sends only opaque IDs to Shopify, with no creator personal data such as names or contact details. The Web Pixel keeps its cookie on your own store's domain. Checkouts happen on your own Shopify, so customer orders stay in your store as they do today.
